title: Animals Including Humans (KS1)
subject: Science
strapline: Animal groups, body parts, senses and staying healthy.
facts: Animals can be sorted into groups: mammals, birds, fish, reptiles, amphibians and insects.
Mammals have fur or hair and feed their babies milk; humans are mammals.
Birds have feathers, wings and a beak; fish have fins, gills and scales and live in water.
Animals can be carnivores (eat meat), herbivores (eat plants) or omnivores (eat both).
Humans have five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
Body parts include head, arms, legs, hands and feet; we can name them on ourselves.
To stay healthy we need exercise, the right food and drink, sleep and good hygiene.

quick_quiz.q: What do we call an animal that eats only plants?
Which animal group has feathers and wings?
Which sense do you use with your ears?

teacher_tips: Sort animal pictures into groups and justify each choice out loud.
Link "staying healthy" to the children's own routines for relevance.
Use a senses walk outdoors to make the five senses concrete.
